query: Historical first-round vote shares of Zambian presidential elections 2011, 2015, 2016, 2021 for incumbents and winners, and accuracy of Zambian pre-election opinion polls versus actual results
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## Zambian Presidential First-Round Vote Shares (2011–2021)

| Election | Winner | Share | Incumbent/Ruling | Runner-up | Margin |
|----------|--------|-------|------------------|-----------|--------|
| **2011** | Sata (PF, challenger) | ~42% | Banda (MMD) lost ~36.1% | Hichilema ~18% | ~6 pts |
| **2015** (by-election) | Lungu (PF, ruling) | 48.33% | — | Hichilema 46.67% | 1.68 pts |
| **2016** | Lungu (PF, incumbent) | 50.35% | won narrowly | Hichilema 47.63% | 2.72 pts |
| **2021** | Hichilema (UPND, challenger) | 57.86% | Lungu (PF) lost 37.34% | — | ~20.5 pts |

**Incumbent takeaway:** Two of three ruling-party incumbents facing a strong challenger were defeated (Banda 2011, Lungu 2021). The identical Lungu–Hichilema matchup swung from a 1.68-pt Lungu win (2015) → 2.72-pt Lungu win (2016) → 20.5-pt Hichilema landslide (2021).

## Polling Accuracy
Zambian pre-election polls have a **poor, volatile record**:
- The most publicized **2021 PSAZ poll called the wrong winner**: predicted Lungu 44.5% / Hichilema 30.3%, when Hichilema actually won by ~20 points (understating him by ~27 pts). Methodologically flawed (5 of 10 provinces, PF-friendly weighting, PR-firm partners).
- **Afrobarometer (Dec 2020)** was the most credible source and correctly signaled PF's collapse (PF 22.9% vs UPND 25.2%, 45.6% undecided).
- The **2015 and 2016 races** were decided within ~3 points — effectively within any poll's margin of error.
- Structural obstacles: strong regional voting blocs, provincial under-sampling, high undecided/refusal rates, social-desirability bias, and turnout volatility (32% in 2015 vs. 61% in 2021).

Full synthesis with all data points and sources has been delivered via the StructuredOutput tool.
